description: Health, throughput, latency, app internals and system metrics for a CPU-only BLIP image captioning app (Streamlit + Prometheus + node_exporter).

options.content:
**Image captioning app (BLIP, CPU only) · Prometheus + node_exporter.** Read from top to bottom: **1 Health** (is everything up?) → **2 Throughput** (how much work?) → **3 Latency** (how fast?) → **4 App internals** → **5 System** (CPU, memory, disk, network) → **6 Correlation** (do bulk ZIP uploads drive the hardware?).

Colours use the Okabe-Ito colour-blind safe palette. Every line also has point markers, and **dashed lines mark bulk (ZIP)** or the second statistic, so the charts still read in black and white or print. Each axis label states its unit and its scale (linear or log₁₀). Hover the ⓘ next to a title for what the panel shows. The horizontal axis of every chart is time, in your browser's time zone. Refresh: 5 s.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard — six rows, health first
1 · Health — is everything up?

panels.description: UP when Prometheus can scrape the app's /metrics endpoint on port 18000. DOWN means the Streamlit app is not running.
panels.title: App status — caption_app scrape target

panels.description: UP when Prometheus can scrape node_exporter on port 9100. Without it the System and Correlation rows are empty.
panels.title: Node exporter status — system metrics

panels.description: LOADED once the captioning model is in memory. NOT LOADED when the app is down or has not loaded the model yet.
panels.title: Model status — BLIP in memory

panels.description: Time since the app process started. Shows 0 s while the app is down, and starts from 0 again after a restart.
panels.title: App uptime — since the process started

panels.description: Failed images divided by all images processed in the last 5 minutes. 0% means every image was captioned.
panels.title: Failed images — last 5 min

panels.description: Running total of successfully captioned images: single uploads and images from ZIP files.
panels.title: Images captioned — total, by mode
2 · Throughput — how much work is the app doing?

panels.description: Images processed per minute over a 1-minute window. Solid = single uploads, dashed = bulk ZIP. Failed images are shown separately.
panels.title: Throughput — images per minute, by mode and result

panels.description: How often users press the buttons: one request per single image, one per ZIP file.
panels.title: Requests — uploads per minute, single images vs ZIP files

panels.description: Requests grouped by the client IP and browser labels. Localhost shows as 127.0.0.1.
panels.title: Requests per client — IP, browser

panels.description: One row per Streamlit session ID (each browser tab gets its own) with its IP, browser, mode and number of requests.
panels.title: Sessions — requests per browser session

panels.description: Total size of uploaded files per minute, from the caption_upload_bytes summary (_sum).
panels.title: Upload volume — bytes received per minute, by mode
3 · Latency — how fast are captions produced?

panels.description: Time the model takes per image, from the caption_inference_seconds histogram. p50 = half of images are faster (solid); p95 = 95% are faster (dashed). Log scale.
panels.title: Inference latency — p50 and p95 per image, by mode

panels.description: Average = total time ÷ number of images over 1 minute (_sum ÷ _count). Inference comes from the histogram, preprocessing (resize) from the summary.
panels.title: Average time per image — inference vs preprocessing, by mode

panels.description: Each column is one minute; each cell counts images whose inference time fell in that bucket. Brighter = more images (Viridis, colour-blind safe, square-root colour scale). The vertical axis lists the histogram buckets in order, evenly spaced (ordinal), not to scale.
panels.title: Latency distribution — images per inference-time bucket

panels.description: Time from pressing 'Caption all images' to the last image, from the caption_bulk_job_seconds histogram over 5 minutes.
panels.title: Bulk job duration — p50 and p95 time to finish one ZIP
4 · App internals — what is the app doing right now?

panels.description: Requests currently being processed (gauge). Above 0 means the CPU is busy captioning.
panels.title: Active requests — in progress right now, by mode

panels.description: Goes up when a ZIP starts and down by one per captioned image. Back to 0 when done.
panels.title: Bulk queue — images still waiting in running ZIP jobs

panels.description: Resident memory (RSS) of the Streamlit process, and the memory added when the BLIP model was loaded.
panels.title: App memory — process vs model load

panels.description: error: bad_image, bad_zip, no_images or inference_error. skipped: files inside a ZIP that are not images, hidden, too large or over the limit.
panels.title: Errors and skipped files — totals since start, by type

panels.description: Average megapixels of uploaded images (left axis) and average words per caption (right axis, dashed), from the two histograms' _sum ÷ _count over 1 minute.
panels.title: Image content — avg size, caption words

panels.description: How long the model took to load, how much memory it added, and how many images were in the most recent ZIP.
panels.title: Model facts — load time, memory, last ZIP

panels.description: From the caption_app Info metric: which model and Python version the app is running.
panels.title: Build info — model, device, version
5 · System — node_exporter: CPU, memory, disk, network

panels.description: Stacked, so the top line is the machine total, the same value as the machine CPU line in row 6. user = programs, system = kernel and interrupts, iowait + steal = waiting for the disk or the host computer, unassigned = busy time that the per-mode counters did not assign to any of these.
panels.title: CPU utilisation — % of all cores, by CPU mode (stacked)

panels.description: Used = total minus available memory. When 'available' gets close to 0 the machine starts swapping.
panels.title: Memory — used vs available

panels.description: How full the main disk is. Model downloads and Prometheus data live here. Orange from 80%, vermillion from 90%.
panels.title: Disk usage — root (/) % full

panels.description: Disk traffic of all physical disks (loop devices excluded). Spikes when the model is loaded from disk.
panels.title: Disk I/O — read vs write rate

panels.description: Network traffic on all interfaces except loopback. Rises during the first model download.
panels.title: Network — receive vs send rate

panels.description: Average number of processes waiting for CPU. Above the 'CPU cores' line the machine is overloaded.
panels.title: Load — 1 and 5 min vs cores
6 · Correlation — do bulk ZIP uploads drive the hardware?

panels.description: When a ZIP is processed, bulk images per minute (dashed, right axis) and machine CPU (solid, left axis) should rise and fall together.
panels.title: Bulk uploads vs CPU — machine CPU % (left) and bulk images per minute (right)

panels.description: CPU used by the Streamlit process (process_cpu_seconds_total) next to CPU used by the whole machine, both as % of all cores. The gap is everything else.
panels.title: Who uses the CPU — caption app vs whole machine (%)

panels.description: Memory used by the Streamlit process next to memory used by the whole machine. The model is loaded once, so app memory should stay flat during bulk jobs.
panels.title: Memory — caption app vs whole machine
